AI tools are incredibly useful for speeding up security tasks, but they shouldn’t replace human judgment. They work best as decision-support systems helping with pattern detection, log analysis, and triage—but their outputs still need validation. Clear boundaries, proper tuning, and continuous human oversight are essential to avoid false positives, blind spots, or over-reliance on automated results.

Over-reliance risk: AI may generate false positives or missed positives. If one relies entirely on AI for decision-making, it may lead security personnel to overlook contextual judgments.

Adversarial attack: Attackers may deceive AI models by poisoning data or designing adversarial samples (for example, allowing malware to evade detection). The security team needs to continuously test the robustness of the AI system.

The combination works well for academic projects where I need to both understand and implement secure code.
